# Synthetic historical 0145 fixtures

These three fixtures were produced by the historical business code before migration 0145,
not generated by current code during CI. They contain only synthetic records. All table
rows, nested JSON, archive DDL and frozen consumer sources were reviewed for privacy.

The monetary fixtures preserve two sales and three cost corrections each. The zero fixture
preserves an entryless zero-value issue; the test posts a real late cost of 100 and checks
25/75 allocation, confirmation and replay. Each restore checks all 151 tables and 102
sequences against its canonical snapshot before applying the real migrations.

`fixtures.json` pins compressed and original bytes. `manifest.json` pins the isolated
consumer originating from commit 83706c062349bfd983933bf58b916b4eba6fbdf8. It contains 37
byte-exact files from the previously accepted projected consumer closure, plus an empty
`core/domain/__init__.py`. Earlier closure projections include closing_commands,
financial_closing, ProcurementDTO and namespace initializers. The commit identifies source
provenance, not an unchanged copy of its entire tree. No further business projection was
introduced here; the producer and fixture generators are excluded. The runner rejects imports from the current checkout. Frozen consumer files are
excluded from Ruff to preserve their original bytes; the runner and maintained helper are linted.

The tests use the existing isolated PostgreSQL 16 service and its standard pg_restore.
Set ACCOUNTING_TEST_POSTGRES_CONTAINER to that service's container ID (CI does this).
The UUID database, host port and master/fixture ownership markers must match before restore.
The helper never starts or stops a container and never targets a production database.
These historical migration tests do not certify the current application schema or release.
